paragraphs: Direct judgment: this job is not about “being able to read a circuit,” but about closing the loop among object, version, engineering instructions, instrument conditions, raw readings, deviations, changes, retests, and acceptance status.

Observable signals: check the object version; keep every reading; do not let an average mask an out-of-range value; stop and escalate when the electrical state, instrument, instructions, or authorization are unclear.

60-minute fictional paper sample: specification 4.90—5.10V, readings 5.02, 5.08, 5.18V; asset E-204, drawing E-240; it passes only if the identity is consistent and every reading is within limits. Do not touch real circuits, instruments, or equipment.

Reference answer: the mean of 5.09V cannot offset the 5.18V reading that is 0.08V out of range, and the identity is contradictory; the record is not closed, so it should be isolated and escalated, and must not be adjusted or released.

Occupational boundary: O*NET 17-3023.00, typically implementing electrical and electronic design support, build, testing, maintenance, adjustment, and recording under the guidance of engineering staff.

entries: Work object: electrical and electronic components, circuits, controls, machinery, drawings, engineering instructions, test equipment, and operating records.
Technical tasks: review plans and specifications, read blueprints, wiring diagrams, and schematics, and assemble, test, or maintain per engineering instructions.
Exception tasks: set up test equipment, identify faults, interpret test information, and repair or modify prototypes; actual execution is constrained by training and authorization.

paragraphs: Complete process: check object version — confirm instructions and plan — check instrument conditions — authorized execution — record readings — compare against specifications — isolate deviations — authorized changes — retest and acceptance.

U.S. work context: 90% email daily, 74% face-to-face discussions daily, 71% indoor controlled environment daily, 85% typically 40 hours per week; some positions also involve field work and protective measures. Survey feedback is not a guarantee of a specific organization's shifts or individual fit.

Preparation level: Job Zone3 (SVP6 to <7), RIC; education feedback 34% associate's degree, 21% college without a degree, 16% high school. BLS indicates typically an associate's degree, but some positions may accept high school or prefer a bachelor's; none of these is a unified Chinese education requirement or a guarantee of safety authorization.
Checkable outputs: object ID, drawing version, configuration, instruments, conditions, readings, criteria, deviations, changes, retest, and acceptance status.
Quality standards: consistent identity and version, clear units and conditions, every reading retained, deviations not masked, changes authorized, and retests not passed off as acceptance.

Adjacent boundary: engineers lean toward research, design, and engineering responsibility; this occupation typically implements, tests, maintains, and produces checkable records under the guidance of engineering staff.
Computer hardware engineers research, design, develop, or test computer and related equipment; this occupation has a broader scope and is typically guided by engineering staff.

Electrical engineers research, design, develop, test, or supervise the manufacturing and installation of electrical equipment and systems; this occupation focuses on implementing and verifying against engineering input.

Electronics engineers (except computer) research, design, develop, and test electronic components and systems; this occupation provides the corresponding build, test, maintenance, and recording support.
Mechanical engineers plan and design mechanical equipment; mechatronics engineers research, design, develop, and test automation, intelligent systems, and industrial controls.
Can assist with: drawing version comparison, bills of materials, log parsing, anomaly flagging, and report drafts.

Conditions for adoption: object IDs, versions, data formats, instrument records, and the permission model are reliable. AI Impact Score 50% is an editorial estimate. Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((75+25+50)/3+0.5)=50; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.The three tasks, ratings and sources are listed in the FermatMind method source record on this page.
Data threshold: retain raw readings, units, conditions, configuration, personnel, and time.
Human control: verify the physical object, wiring, instruments, and measurement conditions, and reproduce anomalies.
Residual responsibility: tools cannot confirm the true energy state, safe entry conditions, or fault causality.
Failure risks: wrong version, wrong units, logs mixed across objects, averages masking out-of-range values, or automatic release.

Editorial trial suggestion: compare drawing/BOM versions, parse logs, and flag anomalies in an authorized environment; keep raw readings and conditions and measure actual accuracy and time on task. No actual adoption rate or efficiency measurement was taken this round.
Conditions for adoption: object ID, version, data format, instrument records, and the permission model are reliable and have been human-reviewed.

No Chinese national wage distribution precisely corresponding to 17-3023 was obtained this round; broad-scope industry averages may be referenced in practice, but they cannot fill in a technician occupation median.

Insufficient evidence: the National Bureau of Statistics materials checked for this page do not provide a Mainland China national single-occupation wage percentile precisely corresponding to O*NET 17-3023.00, reaching only industry and broad job-category framing. Statistical period: the 2025 National Bureau of Statistics materials are published by industry and broad job category and cannot substitute for a precise occupation median.
Measurement framing: annual salary, monthly salary, hourly wage, overtime, allowances, and bonuses must not be mixed.
Use in job seeking: hold region, industry, shift, education and experience, travel, protective measures, instrument responsibility, overtime, and benefits constant.
Market framing: O*NET presents the U.S. national wage for 17-3023.00.
Statistical period: 2025 BLS wage data.
Median: 37.59 USD per hour, 78,190 USD per year, not a starting salary.
Units: hourly and annual wages come from the same source and are not mixed with project quotes or bonuses.

The occupation median within an industry must be kept separate: another OOH industry, semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing, is 73,460 USD/year (May 2025); it does not represent the overall industry average.

The 10/50/90 percentiles are 49,510/78,190/115,700 USD/year; the 25/75 percentiles were not obtained this round and are not interpolated. Statistics are not an individual quote, a hiring guarantee, or an income guarantee.
Fit depends on whether you can link object and version, engineering input, measurement conditions, deviations, and acceptance status into a traceable chain.
Positive signal: proactively checks the object and drawing version, keeps every reading and condition, and stops and escalates when the electrical state or authorization is unclear.
Positive signal: can steadily complete supervised testing per drawings and engineering instructions and records units, conditions, and instrument status item by item.
Caution signal: unwilling to record measurement conditions or accept review, and prone to using an average to mask a single out-of-range point.
Verification action: complete this page's paper questions and do the two variants, “change the label to E-240” and “change the third reading to 5.06V”.
Use a checkable test record and deviation form to verify whether engineering input — measurement — deviation — retest are linked into a chain.
Use a record sheet covering one continuous week to verify willingness to maintain raw readings, units, versions, and change records.
Preference descriptions are not capability conclusions: use actual testing and troubleshooting tasks to observe whether you prefer instrument operation or drawing and document organization.
Electrical/energy storage: real wiring, testing, repair, and calibration are carried out only per employer procedures, engineering instructions, protective measures, and position authorization.
Object/version: isolate the affected work when labels, drawings, configurations, or work orders are inconsistent.
Measurement quality: when instrument status, units, conditions, or per-reading values are missing, an average must not be substituted.

Energy boundary: where U.S. 1910.147 applies and maintenance may involve unexpected energization or release of stored energy, follow the employer's energy control procedure and have only authorized personnel perform it.
Common rule: if any of the electrical state, instrument, instructions, authorization, deviation, retest, or acceptance is unclear, stop the affected steps, record, and escalate.
Practical entry point: start with object and version checks, test records, units and conditions, acceptance criteria, deviation forms, and handover summaries.
Employer evidence: verify education and experience, test equipment training, electrical safety, energy control, engineering changes, return to service, and acceptance authorization.
Portfolio without experience: complete this page's paper questions and show the mean, the single out-of-range point, the identity contradiction, and the status.
Interview and probation: explain why a passing mean cannot cover the 5.18V out-of-range value and why the E-204/E-240 contradiction cannot be ignored.

Seven-day trial: copy the rules, build a record sheet, compute the mean deviation, draw the closed loop, make the label variant, make the reading variant, and review the stop conditions — one day each.
Qualification decisions: verify wiring, energization testing, instruments, repair and calibration, energy isolation, quality determination, return to service, and engineering release item by item.

The three directions and four stages are an editorial example of competence development, not a unified job ladder: first stabilize versions and records, then assemble and test under supervision, and gradually take on troubleshooting, changes, and handover within authorization; promotion is checked against position requirements.
Transition paths: hardware, electrical, electronics, mechanical, or mechatronics engineering paths require added higher-level design analysis, education, and responsibility evidence.

career_risk_cards.boundary: This page cannot replace the employer's energy control procedures, work permits, or applicable law.
career_risk_cards.direct_answer: First identify five categories of risk: electrical and stored-energy state, object and version, measurement quality, energy control authorization, and acceptance boundaries.
career_risk_cards.evidence_scope: The risks and measures are an editorial summary; O*NET supports the task context, and 1910.147 supports the hazardous energy boundary for applicable machine maintenance, not incident rates or a complete electrical work standard.
career_risk_cards.heading: Risks and control points for Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians

risks.consequence: Can cause electric shock, arc flash, or equipment damage and change accident responsibility.
risks.mitigation: Carry out per the employer's electrical safety and energy control procedures, protective measures, and position authorization applicable to the specific work; 1910.147 does not cover all electrical exposure, and this page is not an operating instruction.
risks.scenario: The energy state is not confirmed during real wiring, testing, repair, or calibration.

risks.affected_roles: Assembly, testing, and drawing execution position
risks.consequence: Can lead to testing the wrong object, making conclusions incomparable and affecting release decisions.
risks.mitigation: Check the object and drawing version and, on conflict, isolate the affected work and hand it to engineering or an authorized role for confirmation.
risks.scenario: Labels, drawings, configuration, or work order versions do not match the physical object.

risks.consequence: May use an average to mask a single out-of-range point and produce a false pass conclusion.
risks.mitigation: Keep every raw reading and condition, compare item by item against acceptance criteria, and record out-of-range items separately and retest.
risks.scenario: Instrument status, units, measurement conditions, or per-reading values are missing.

risks.affected_roles: Equipment maintenance and energy isolation position
risks.consequence: In U.S. maintenance scenarios where 29 CFR 1910.147 applies, this can cause personal injury.
risks.mitigation: Follow the employer's energy control procedures, with lockout/tagout performed only by authorized personnel; the provision has scope limits and exceptions.
risks.scenario: During maintenance, unexpected energization or release of stored energy may occur while authorization is unclear.

risks.consequence: May let unverified changes enter delivery and amplify quality and safety risk.
risks.mitigation: Retest per process and record, have engineering or an authorized role confirm acceptance, and do not release on your own beyond your authority.
risks.scenario: After handling a deviation, it is treated as complete without retesting or confirmation by an authorized role.

risks.affected_roles: Electrical and Electronic Engineering Technologists and Technicians
risks.consequence: Can cause irreversible safety or compliance consequences.
risks.mitigation: Stop the affected steps, record the status, and escalate per the employer's authorization chain.
risks.scenario: Encountering wiring, energization, change, or release tasks beyond your authorized scope.
risks.title: Responsibility boundaries
